direction.concept: A familiar evening room made by the underside of a bridge. A wide, low eye-level scene makes the screening and the nearby director conversation immediately recognizable.
direction.substantive_non_glyph_visual: A long cropped bridge soffit, a luminous outdoor film screen on the left, adults seated on several mats, and a standing adult with a microphone beside the screen. Creek-side paving continues across the image; this is an evocative setting rather than an asserted architectural likeness of Yeongagyo.
direction.expression_system: One continuous cinematic environmental image. Keep believable body proportions, quiet dusk illumination and a broad horizontal architectural crop; the screen and listening bodies create the event, rather than a decorative object.
direction.copy_visual_relationship: First gaze: the lit screen and shared audience. Next useful information: date and time in the right opening. All type occupies a calm unpictured portion of the arch, with a clean boundary before people and screen light.
direction.whole_visual_layout: At 720×405, the environmental scene occupies roughly the left 60% and continues behind the upper bridge edge. Reserve the right 36% as a dark, nearly uniform opening. Put identity at its top, schedule in its middle, participation beneath; keep every block inside the arch opening and above the lower crop.
direction.typography_plan: Korean title 32–36 px, broken at the word boundary into two lines; English 17–19 px. Descriptor and all practical entries at least 17 px, schedule 21–26 px. Use clear contemporary Korean sans, left alignment, compact but open line spacing and a common vertical edge. Keep the descriptor on one horizontal line at 17-18 px within the approximately259px opening, rather than allocating two lines. If the actual font cannot fit it, expand only identity to y4-42%, schedule to y45-68%, and guidance to y72-96%; preserve readable type.
direction.color_material_emotion: Deep blue dusk and natural warm screen light establish an approachable adult evening. Light text on the dark information opening has firm contrast; the scene carries restrained photographic detail without a glossy portrait treatment.
direction.distinction: With color and material removed, M1 is a distant horizontal environment with an information opening at the right; M4 uses huge foreground bodies at both edges and a central vertical information corridor. M1's image describes the venue arrangement before a person's gesture.

reference_observations.observed_principle: The personally viewed cached image sets a physical frame and a folded, worn object against a broad pale field. The frame intersects informational lines; sparse space, restrained color and visible object edges act together.
reference_observations.current_request_application: Let a real scene boundary—the bridge opening—determine where image ends and readable information begins. Use spatial depth and a generous quiet field, rather than transplanting the frame, object, distressed surface or original title.

reference_observations.observed_principle: Root's actual preview observations report a landscape image/information division, separate date/time and place groups, and heavy practical type linking an event to a performer image.
reference_observations.current_request_application: Give the event scene and participation facts immediately legible adjoining territories, while choosing a continuous bridge space, a different proportion and a different information route.

direction.positive_construction: Compose the long soffit and screen first, place the seated audience and microphone-bearing speaker in the same coherent space, then fit the three right-side text groups to the actual Korean line lengths.

copy_groups.position_relationship: Right opening, upper4-38%; two-line Korean title, English, then the full descriptor on one line at17-18px. If real line fit requires it, use identity y4-42%, schedule y45-68%, guidance y72-96%.
Right opening, middle 42–65%; date, larger time, then venue, all sharing the identity's left edge.
Right opening, lower 69–96%; four clearly separated lines, with enough width to preserve the complete free-admission entry.

common_constraints: Print every supplied entry exactly once, with readable Korean/English and intact punctuation; no added text, logos, pseudo-print, watermark or QR.
Each result is one separate flat opaque landscape16:9 poster, not a stretched/cropped portrait or a contact sheet.
Five genuinely distinct complete visual systems, composition, image/type roles and impressions, beyond material/filter/palette changes.
Substantive content-grounded nonglyph visual construction required; type/whitespace-only, tiny icon/texture and glyph-model-only loopholes prohibited.
Outdoor short-film screening and conversation must be recognizable, with an approachable adult cultural-event tone. All supplied practical information must be readable at usage720.
